newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania's top court delays Heidnik's execution.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania's top court delays Heidnik's execution.

text.p: - Killer Gary Heidnik was moved from an execution holding cell back to death row Saturday after the Pennsylvania Supreme Court blocked his execution until it can hear arguments on his mental competence.
The order calls for lawyers to file briefs Monday and for a hearing to start Wednesday.
That means the current death warrant would expire at 12:01 a.m. Sunday. Gov. Tom Ridge does not plan to sign another warrant until Pennsylvania's high court acts.

The state court will be taking up the same issue that three levels of federal courts disagreed upon earlier -- whether Heidnik was able to make a rational decision to forgo appeals of his death sentence.
Heidnik's execution was delayed several times by legal wrangling last week, the most recent late Friday night.
Convicted of kidnapping and torturing six women, two of them fatally, a decade ago, he would have been the third person to die since the state reinstated the death penalty.
Heidnik, 53, claimed insanity at his 1988 trial, but a jury convicted him and sentenced him to death.
The strange case came to public attention within hours after Josefina Rivera escaped from a North Philadelphia rowhouse March 24, 1987.

She had been shackled with five other women in the cellar, which Heidnik had converted into a torture chamber where he enticed streetwalkers into his home to make them his sex slaves. One was killed, and a second died of starvation and mistreatment.
Police records show Deborah Dudley's body was found near a rural road in New Jersey. She had been electrocuted.
Sandra Lindsay's body was found carved into parts in a basement refrigerator. Heidnik had cooked some parts and fed them to his captives, mixed with dog food, the four survivors testified.
